report:
Reviewed complete rustc_execution claim against all three ordinary implementation entries (metadata.rs, compile/mod.rs, compile/rustc.rs) and all five associated test bodies. No TODO/N/A entries exist. The metadata implementation uses the sysroot embedded by sage-host/build.rs and derives bin/rustc from it. The adapter invokes that binary with the same sysroot, the materialized src/lib.rs in the fixture project, its edition, crate-type lib, emit metadata, and no target/test/feature overrides; the default target is the compiler host. Only the compiler process is launched, never the produced fixture. Thus metadata-only/no-runtime behavior follows directly from the fixed command construction. prepare writes the same files used by Sage, unconditionally invokes rustc, holds its result while opening and checking Sage, then combines both failures. There is no opt-out field. Metadata loading skips building a dependency-free local fixture, so negative fixtures reach Sage. Query events are cleared after host setup; rustc runs outside Sage context/query capture. Captured observe::collect confirms the captured event list comes from Sage checking.

The pinned_rustc_checks_errors_editions_and_normal_library_configuration test proves actual compiler checking via a type error, matching expected source errors and overflow, differing IntoFuture prelude behavior in editions 2024/2021, and invalid cfg(test)/feature bodies remaining disabled. The mandatory-rustc integration test proves a rustc-only warning causes preparation failure despite no Sage diagnostic, succeeds with the rustc-qualified warning, and accepts matched deny errors. The multi-file both_compilers_report_source_errors_from_materialized_modules test explicitly asserts both Sage and Rustc error reports and child source path, detecting early return after either source failure and proving the child file is checked. It passed.

parse rejects non-JSON, malformed records, unexpected severity, and invalid source offsets, as asserted by malformed_compiler_output_and_invalid_fixture_offsets_fail. execute maps a failed process spawn into preparation failure. validate_output rejects non-UTF-8 stderr, unexpected stdout, malformed JSON and any status/error combination other than success/no errors or exit 1/errors. The new Unix infrastructure test invokes a nonexistent compiler path, then injects exit 0 with reported errors, exit 1 without errors, exit 2 with errors, signal termination, malformed JSON, invalid UTF-8 and unexpected stdout, asserting the specific infrastructure failure messages. Its successful empty output control also passes. Signal/status simulation is explicitly Unix-gated; portable parser and real rustc tests remain unconditional. Existing real negative fixtures cover accepted exit 1/error combinations. The extraction of execute and validate_output preserves the pinned production command and introduces no public configuration bypass.

Commands executed: cargo fmt; cargo test -p sage-test-harness execution_review_tests (2 passed); cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib rustc (10 passed, including all five associated tests); cargo build (passed with existing warnings). An earlier exact short-name filter selected zero tests and is not counted as validation. Additional dependencies were captured with review read: build.rs, annotations.rs, and observe.rs collection/matching regions. Essential pinning metadata association was added; build.rs is explicitly captured because build-script associations are not inventoried as library implementations. Fresh review start followed all edits. This assessment covers inspection and the recorded commands, not an unperformed cross-platform run. Independent post-codegen/sanity checks are coordinated centrally.
